headline: CABOMETYX growth continues, buybacks squeeze cash
summary_short: Exelixis reported Q1 FY2026 revenue of $610.8M (+10.0% y/y) and diluted EPS of $0.79 (+43.6% y/y), while $430.4M in share buybacks pulled quarter-end cash down 53.1% q/q to $226.2M.
summary_long: Total revenues rose 10.0% y/y to $610.8M, driven by ~7% higher CABOMETYX unit sales in RCC/NET and a 1% price increase, plus higher Ipsen royalties and a Takeda milestone payment. R&D expenses fell 5.8% y/y on lower clinical-trial and manufacturing costs, partly offset by higher drug-discovery licensing costs; SG&A rose 1.8% y/y on zanzalintinib launch-prep marketing. Net income grew 31.9% y/y to $210.5M ($0.79 diluted EPS) as revenue growth outpaced flat operating expenses and the effective tax rate eased to 21.4% from 22.4%. The company paid $430.4M toward its buyback program, cutting cash to $226.2M (-53.1% q/q) and equity to $1.936B. No formal FY2026 guidance was issued; zanzalintinib's colorectal-cancer NDA remains under FDA review, PDUFA December 3, 2026.

drivers.explanation: CABOMETYX units sold grew ~7% y/y on continued RCC/NET demand and refill volume, plus a 1% average price increase; collaboration revenue also rose on higher Ipsen royalties and a Takeda commercial milestone.
Decrease was primarily due to lower clinical-trial and manufacturing costs for development candidates, partially offset by higher drug-discovery-related license and collaboration costs.
Increase was primarily due to marketing ahead of the anticipated zanzalintinib launch, higher legal and advisory fees, and personnel costs, partially offset by lower corporate giving.
Growth is explained by revenue +10.0% y/y against roughly flat total operating expenses (-2.5% y/y), lifting operating income +34.5%, plus a lower effective tax rate (21.4% vs 22.4%).
Decline was primarily due to $430.4M of cash paid to repurchase common stock under the buyback program, partially offset by cash generated from product sales and collaborations.

FDA accepted the zanzalintinib NDA for previously treated metastatic colorectal cancer with a PDUFA target action date of December 3, 2026; no numeric FY2026 financial guidance range was issued in this filing.
